findings.evidence: “Shell variables do not survive between tool calls” restates shell behavior; the useful instruction is to reuse the resolved absolute path so a stale installation cannot take precedence.
findings.fix: Keep the sibling-first lookup and the instruction to substitute the printed absolute path in every invocation. Record removal of the generic shell explanation.

findings.evidence: “set up a cross-AI execution runner” identifies setup, but the description does not explicitly distinguish configuring a runner from asking it to execute or review a plan now.
findings.fix: Use this skill to set up or migrate a project's GSD `.planning/config.json` without the full `gsd-settings` interview. Recommend model tiers, wire installed skills to GSD agents, and preview and apply cross-AI plan review or execution settings. Also use it to render or upgrade `cross-ai.mjs`, run `ensure-runner`, or merge `cross-ai.mjs.new`. Use `gsd-config` for advanced or integration settings and the cross-AI dispatch skill to run or troubleshoot a live lane.

findings.evidence: The full runner exit-code mapping loads with the prerequisites even when neither execution nor a stop is in scope, and runner.md says “see the policy reference” without identifying it at the migration step.
findings.fix: Keep the warning to interpret the runner's status rather than its exit code in SKILL.md. Move the detailed mapping to references/runner.md under the existing non-ok-status trigger, and give retry migration and tuning a direct conditional pointer to the sibling cross-AI skill's references/subprocess-quota-policy.md.

findings.evidence: The mandatory approval step names the config diff rows but does not require showing the runner artifact preview or obtaining informed approval for full-permission execution. The permission disclosure is separated from the point where the user approves.
findings.fix: At step 4, include the runner artifact outcome and, when enabling execution, disclose that the v2 hook lets the selected runtime act with full permissions. Require approval of that consequence along with the config rows; if the owner declines, disable execution in the plan and show a new dry run.

findings.evidence: The router-only case expects the agent to “choose[] models per tier from the routers available,” but evals/02-opencode-routers-no-catalog.md says the intended fixture has no tier candidates and the agent must surface `needs_choice`. The JSON case supplies neither that inventory nor scripted answers.
findings.fix: Attach a deterministic routers-only inventory and assert that unresolved tier choices are shown, no tier model is invented, and real apply does not run. Use a v1 fixture with real managed override keys for the migration case so its assertions can detect a silent removal.

findings.evidence: The suite has eight positives and eight negatives, but negatives such as “write a README for my personal dotfiles repository” and the Kubernetes autoscaler query do not probe the boundary with adjacent GSD or cross-AI workflows.
findings.fix: Replace several unrelated negatives with requests to tune an advanced GSD setting, configure a provider in opencode.json, execute an already-configured GSD phase, or run a cross-AI review now. Add an indirect positive that asks to give the planner and executor different models without naming the curated flow.

findings.evidence: “Apply only after the user answers” does not bind the write to the preview. apply.py:805–839 rereads the live config and recomputes the writes, so an intervening config change can turn a previewed keep into an unapproved overwrite even though the inventory digest still matches.
findings.fix: Bind apply to the approved preview and an expected pre-write state for the config and runner. Refuse when either has changed, then regenerate the preview and obtain fresh approval. Until the CLI enforces that binding, rerun and compare the preview immediately after approval and disclose that this does not eliminate concurrent edits.

findings.evidence: “On an offline or no-write request, do not run it” correctly blocks inventory, but the flow offers only relaxing the limit. It does not route an offline user who has already supplied a usable inventory, the branch exercised by evals/02-opencode-routers-no-catalog.md.
findings.fix: Distinguish offline from no-write: for an offline request, accept an existing inventory for the same trusted project and proceed to local recommendation without refreshing it; for a strict no-write request, do not run recommend even with an inventory, because it writes plan.json.

findings.evidence: “route tuning questions to `gsd-settings --advanced`” conflicts with the installed GSD command definitions: gsd-settings routes to ordinary settings, while gsd-config owns the `--advanced` and `--integrations` routes.
findings.fix: Route advanced tuning to `/gsd-config --advanced` and integrations to `/gsd-config --integrations`, using the equivalent command syntax on the active host.

findings.evidence: “writes stay inside the project dir plus `/tmp` and `$TMPDIR`, which workspace-write always allows” overstates the boundary. OpenAI documents configurable additional writable roots and exclusions for both temp locations. SKILL.md:234–236 repeats the same fixed-scope claim.
findings.fix: In both locations, say that the v1 hook requests Codex `workspace-write`, not a fixed path allowlist. Cite https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference and https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security with the verification date; tell the agent to verify effective writable roots and protected paths before promising a boundary.

findings.evidence: “pi sets `PI_PROVIDER` and `PI_MODEL` only for commands the pi agent runs through its own bash tool” drives the empty-candidate recovery branch but has no dated upstream source or live check.
findings.fix: Tie the rule to the applicable Pi release and cite its official Bash-tool implementation at a pinned revision with the date checked. Keep the recovery instruction to rerun inventory through the agent Bash tool or decline the steer.

findings.evidence: “`opencode run --standalone` (accepted by opencode v2.0.31)” gives a vendor flag and release claim without a dated source or a live check. The official CLI guide confirms the private-server purpose, not the stated historical compatibility by itself.
findings.fix: Keep the distinction between the standalone runner and the shared-service model lookup. Cite https://opencode.ai/docs/cli with the date checked for the flag's purpose and cite dated v2.0.31 help output for the release claim, or direct the agent to verify flag support using the installed CLI's help.
